blocks.content: The Delhi Sultanate refers to the period when Muslim rulers ruled large parts of India from Delhi between 1206 CE and 1526 CE. It was established after the decline of the Ghurid Empire in India.
1. Foundation of the Delhi Sultanate

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Delhi Sultanate was ruled by five successive dynasties: Slave (Mamluk), Khilji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, and Lodi.
Qutb ud-Din Aibak founded the Sultanate in 1206 AD, while Iltutmish consolidated administration and introduced the Turkan-i-Chahalgani.
Alauddin Khilji introduced market regulation, price controls, and the military practice of Dagh (branding horses) and Chehra (descriptive roll).
Muhammad bin Tughlaq implemented ambitious experiments including token currency and shifting the capital to Daulatabad.
The Delhi Sultanate ended in 1526 AD when Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat.

blocks.content: • Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 CE).
• After Muhammad Ghori's death, his general Qutb-ud-din Aibak established the Delhi Sultanate.
• The Delhi Sultanate officially began in 1206 CE
2. Dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate
3. Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty
• Founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1206.
• He started the construction of Qutub Minar.
• Iltutmish consolidated the Delhi Sultanate and introduced the Iqta system.
• Razia Sultan was the first and only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
• Balban strengthened the central administration and introduced the policy of 'Blood and Iron'.
4. Khilji Dynasty
• Founded by Jalal-ud-din Khilji.
• Alauddin Khilji was the most powerful ruler of this dynasty.
• He introduced important market control reforms.
• He successfully defended India against Mongol invasions.
• He conducted military campaigns in South India.

The Delhi Sultanate established Islamic political rule in northern India, bringing profound administrative, architectural, and socioeconomic transformations across five historic dynasties from 1206 to 1526 AD.
5. Tughlaq Dynasty
• Founded by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.
• Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced many administrative experiments.
• He attempted to shift the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad.
• He introduced token currency which failed.
• Firoz Shah Tughlaq built canals, gardens and many public works.
6. Sayyid Dynasty
• Founded by Khizr Khan in 1414.
• They ruled Delhi after the invasion of Timur.
• This dynasty was politically weak.
7. Lodi Dynasty

rows: Introduction of Chahalgani system, construction of Qutub Minar and Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque.
Market control system, price regulation, creation of military department and Dagh/Chehra systems.
Capital transfer attempt to Daulatabad, introduction of token currency, extensive canal construction.
Established in the aftermath of Timur's invasion of Delhi in 1398 AD.
First Afghan dynasty of Delhi; founding of Agra by Sikandar Lodi.

blocks.content: • Founded by Bahlul Lodi.
• It was the first Afghan dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.
• Sikandar Lodi strengthened administration and founded the city of Agra.
• Ibrahim Lodi was the last ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
• He was defeated by Babur in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
8. Administration of the Delhi Sultanate
9. Economy and Society
• Agriculture was the backbone of the economy.
• Land revenue was the main source of income.
• Trade and commerce developed during this period.
• New towns and markets emerged.
10. Architecture

items: Qutub Minar construction was initiated by Qutb ud-Din Aibak and completed by Shams ud-Din Iltutmish.
Balban established the military department 'Diwan-i-Arz' and introduced the court rituals of Sijda and Paibos.
Agra was founded by Sikandar Lodi in 1504 AD, who also made it his capital in 1506 AD.
The First Battle of Panipat (1526 AD) marked the end of the Lodi Dynasty and the beginning of the Mughal Empire.

blocks.content: • Qutub Minar is one of the most famous monuments of the Delhi Sultanate.
• Alai Darwaza was built by Alauddin Khilji.
• Tughlaq architecture is known for its massive structures.
SSC Exam Important Facts
• Delhi Sultanate began in 1206 CE.
• Qutb-ud-din Aibak founded the Slave Dynasty.
• Razia Sultan was the only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
• Alauddin Khilji introduced market control reforms.
• The Delhi Sultanate ended after the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
